author: agent
text:
Re-read after 0.54.1. The confirms below still hold in substance; they went stale because this module gained a function.

New here: unsuperseded_stale(knowledge) -> list, placed deliberately alongside stamp_for and accepted_for because it is the third rule of the same family - stamp_for is the ONE write-side rule, accepted_for the ONE read-side rule, and this is the ONE ring rule. Per channel, only the NEWEST entry decides. Entries are append-only and never deleted, so without this a coordinate that went coral once stays coral forever no matter how many times somebody answers it (measured: 12 rings on this repo's own map that no amount of fresh confirmation could clear).

It returns rows, not a bool, because two callers want two shapes of the same answer: viz.has_unsuperseded_stale asks "draw a ring?" and delegates here, and query.verify_change asks "WHICH entries did this change invalidate?". Do not let either grow its own copy - the ring and the staleness report must not be able to disagree about what "stale" means, and a second copy of a rule is exactly how 0.53.2's behind-count shipped without the exclusion the dirty check already had.

Order is file order, which is append order. That matters if .coord/meta/**/*.jsonl ever gets a git merge=union driver: union can interleave two people's appends, and "newest" here means last line, not latest ts. Sorting by ts on read would make union safe; until then, be careful what merge strategy you give these files.

author: agent
text:
Re-read after 0.54.2. The confirm below still holds; this module gained the write-side fix.

stamp_for now takes an optional repo_root and, when given one, derives the hash from the WORKING TREE rather than from the entity handed in. The entity always came from the map - a snapshot of the last index - so stamping from it produced notes that were BORN STALE. Measured end to end: edit, let the pre-commit hook name the note you staled, supersede exactly as instructed, re-index, and the brand-new note reads stale=True. Superseding as told healed nothing unless you happened to re-index first, which nothing tells you to do.

_current_entity reuses index(persist=False) - the in-memory path from 0.54.1 - deliberately, rather than re-parsing one file by hand. A second parse path here is precisely how stamp_for and agent_meta drifted apart the first time, one stamping body_hash and the other logic_hash. One definition of what a logic hash is, or the two decay at different rates again.

GhostEntity is raised when the ref resolves in the map but not in the tree. Do not soften it into a fallback: a note stamped against a vanished entity can never be fresh and can never be superseded, and it sits on a coordinate the code has abandoned. Refusing costs one re-index; guessing costs a note that silently means nothing.

The read side is unchanged - accepted_for still admits both tiers so pre-stamp_for entries stay valid - and unsuperseded_stale is still the one ring rule, now also feeding the ambient knowledge_lag warning.

author: cli
text: Re-confirmed after 0.54.2's display work. Two functions now carry the reading rules: for_display sets the human-facing order (newest first) and marks non-deciding entries superseded; unsuperseded_stale reads that flag instead of deriving 'newest' from list position. The pairing is the point - the moment display order flipped, a positional rule would have inverted silently and called a coordinate fresh on the strength of a note somebody had already replaced. Flags survive reordering; positions do not.
